note: Faithful rendering of MMK 23.24-25 with commentary and the opening verses of ch. 24 (24.1-6) plus the start of the commentary; notes are reasonable.

errors.english: is solely included within the cognition that possesses the unimpeded capacity to generate form
errors.why: It is the cause (of the taste) that possesses the unimpeded capacity to produce form; the cognition is a cognition OF that cause, not a cognition possessing the capacity.

note: A sound rendering of a dense Pramāṇa argument on inferring form from taste; one misattached qualifier at the opening.

errors.english: the foundational master of the Middle Way school, circa 2nd century CE
errors.why: The verse simply says 'Nāgārjuna holds thus'; the description and dating are unmarked translator additions inside a verse line.

note: Verses from the Yuktiṣaṣṭikā, MMK 15.6 and the Cārvāka verse are rendered faithfully; only unmarked explanatory insertions intrude.

errors.english: Then, having requested the Bhagavan, and following his command, the monk [note: Sudatta/Anathapindada] went to the city of Shravasti together with Shariputra.
errors.why: The monk is Śāriputra, sent by the Buddha's command to accompany Anāthapiṇḍada (Skt. tadādiṣṭena sahitaḥ śāriputreṇa bhikṣuṇā); Anāthapiṇḍada is a layman, not a monk.

fix.find: Then, having requested the Bhagavan, and following his command, the monk [note: Sudatta/Anathapindada] went to the city of Shravasti together with Shariputra.
fix.replace: Then, having taken leave of the Bhagavan, he [note: Anathapindada] went to the city of Shravasti together with the monk Shariputra, who was assigned to him by the Bhagavan's command.

note: The Jetavana narrative is otherwise faithful; the bilingual Sanskrit lines duplicate the Tibetan and are rightly not translated twice.

errors.english: If you claim that the "ultimate" is an object of interest for one who desires it, then it is merely a desire.
errors.why: The first horn of the dilemma is conceded: if 'ultimate' means taking the ultimate as object through devoted interest (adhimukti), 'that is simply accepted' (འདོད་པ་ཁོ་ན); only the path-of-seeing horn is then attacked.

fix.find: If you claim that the "ultimate" is an object of interest for one who desires it, then it is merely a desire.
fix.replace: If by "ultimate" you mean that it takes the ultimate as its object through devoted interest (adhimukti), that we simply accept.

note: The path-stage similes are rendered correctly; the refutation of the other commentators misreads its concession, and inline unmarked glosses are frequent.

errors.english: all the specific qualities of a brindled cow
errors.why: ཁྱད་པར་ here are the particular individuals (the spotted cow and the others), all of which are unmixed with horse, not the qualities of one brindled cow.

note: A generally sound rendering of the apoha discussion; the trailing 'one line of text follows' is a stray artefact rather than translation.
Faithful rendering of the sūtra passage on the karmic results of slandering the two Dharma-preaching monks; hells and figures are correct.
Faithful rendering of the Daśabhūmika citation and the discussion of ignorance and the view associated with it.

errors.english: Thus, in the absence of that [note: happiness]
errors.why: The 'that' whose absence lets suffering be felt as pleasure is the habituated fear just mentioned, not happiness; the note makes the sentence incoherent.

note: The argument on habituation, pleasure and suffering is followed correctly; one misleading bracketed referent.

errors.english: Does one intend to establish the act of speaking itself as an independent thesis
errors.why: The question is whether 'being a speaker' (vaktṛtva) is put forward as the reason in an independent (svatantra) proof or in a prasaṅga; it is the probans, not a thesis to be established.

errors.english: if one does not analyze it, it appears pleasant; but
errors.why: 'Pleasing only when unexamined' qualifies the mere scripture (āgama) on which the property is known to the opponent; it is not a remark that the prasaṅga itself looks pleasant.

note: The thread of the Tattvasaṃgraha commentary is followable, but the logical vocabulary of the svatantra/prasaṅga dilemma is misparsed in places.
